children: Mexico remains the key growth opportunity for Ternium
, while Argentina is its weak spot, analysts at J.P. Morgan wrote in a note on Thursday after a meeting with the Latin American steelmaker's senior management.

The firm expects the first slab from its Pesqueria steelmaking complex in northern Mexico to come in February and it forecasts an annual slab production between 2.6 and 2.7 metric tons once the facility reaches full capacity, the brokerage added.
Ternium characterized the next two years at the plant as a  capital-light phase to ramp up new facilities and develop new grades, J.P. Morgan noted

Mexico would remain Ternium's top capital allocation priority, thanks to its trade protections, government infrastructure spending and the role of USMCA in supporting regional manufacturing integration
The firm expects the USMCA trade pact to be renewed with adjustments and views a bilateral Section 232 agreement as a potential intermediate step
A resolution could help narrow the Mexico-US steel price gap, Ternium reportedly said
Assets in Brazil have a solid industrial base, and the country is gradually taking trade measures, but not to the same degree as the United States and Mexico
Argentina is the weak spot, with construction and overall consumption very low and traditional manufacturers under pressure from Chinese imports
On dividends, management pointed to the $0.90 payout declared last November but said an increase was possible
